RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 50

An all-male panel in engineering often reflects industry demographics rather than intentional discrimination. However, combined with your substantial experience advantage (15 years versus 8) and unanswered follow-up, affinity bias is a plausible factor. Leadership roles also heavily weight client relationships and business development over technical tenure.

Whether to raise it depends on your objective. Do not raise the panel's gender when seeking feedback from the firm; alleging bias without evidence prompts defensiveness and burns bridges. Instead, politely request a verbal debrief on objective selection criteria. Only raise panel demographics if you consult an employment attorney or pursue a formal discrimination complaint, where composition and qualification disparities serve as relevant circumstantial evidence.
